source.title: Scale Efficiently: Insights from Pre-training and Fine-tuning Transformers
source.authors: Yi Tay; Mostafa Dehghani; J. Rao; W. Fedus; Samira Abnar; Hyung Won Chung; Sharan Narang; Dani Yogatama; A. Vaswani; Donald Metzler

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own scaling experiments and argues that pretraining and downstream scaling behave differently, with downstream results depending on model shape and compute region.
record.gate_note: The paper measures pretraining negative log-perplexity and downstream scores while varying model sizes and shapes. It does not fit power laws or report a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its ViT experiments compare DeepNarrow and base configurations but do not test whether a power-law form holds in vision.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own T5 pretraining and fine-tuning over 200+ configurations (5M–30B params). It reports upstream negative log-perplexity against model size and shape, which bears on V1 qualitatively and on V4. It argues explicitly that downstream fine-tuned performance is not predictable from size or pretraining perplexity among nearby sizes, which bears on V6. It fits no power laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state they confirm Kaplan's upstream finding of strong size dependence and weak shape dependence. They argue pretraining perplexity can mislead model choice downstream, that scaling-knob effects differ across compute regions, and that T5-Base/Large are Pareto-inefficient. They recommend DeepNarrow (depth-first) scaling, which matches downstream quality with ~50% fewer parameters and ~40% faster training, within hardware limits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses T5 encoder-decoder models pretrained with span-based masked language modeling on C4 for 219 steps, rather than testing autoregressive language-model cross-entropy power laws or fitting scaling exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ between upstream pretraining and downstream fine-tuning, across compute regions, and across scaling knobs; the authors specifically report depth as influential for downstream Pareto efficiency.

fits_no_version.finding: At similar parameter counts, model shape, especially depth, strongly affects downstream fine-tuned accuracy even though upstream loss is nearly shape-independent. Some knobs help downstream but not upstream (e.g. FF2K).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture shape matters little for pretraining loss but substantially for downstream fine-tuned performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The Pareto effect of scaling knobs (depth, width, d_model, heads, d_kv) differs across compute regions (Small/Base/Large starting points, Figure 2). Small-scale scaling strategies may not transfer to larger scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal shape-scaling strategies for downstream efficiency are compute-region dependent.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the relevant results and does not fit or compare power-law exponents. The main pretraining setup uses a limited 219-step schedule and a span-masked encoder-decoder objective, rather than autoregressive language modeling. Figure 1's model-size trend is described qualitatively, without fit statistics.
record.rows_left_out: The many individual configurations in Figures 2 and 3 and appendix Figures 5–8 are not separately extracted; the paper mainly describes their Pareto-frontier and scaling-knob patterns in aggregate, and they do not test power-law fitting or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Table 4's GLUE and SQuAD columns are omitted; the reported AVG downstream score is retained for each listed alternative.

untested.parts: Power-law functional form and exponents; scaling in tokens and compute; autoregressive loss (the objective is span-masked MLM).
All: no small-run fit is used to predict larger runs.
All: the ViT and fine-tuning results compare DeepNarrow configurations and fit no power law.
All: no comparison of fitted exponents or fitting choices. The compute-region dependence concerns shape strategies, not exponents.

missing.what: The Table 4 'Ppl (C4)' upstream column for every configuration. It bears on V4: e.g. Small 32EL (143M) has -1.897 vs Small 16L (134M) -1.825, a sizable shape effect on loss for encoder-only depth. It also provides the loss-vs-downstream pairing needed for V6.
DeepNarrow Small-24L vs T5-Base on 12 extra tasks: the smaller model ties or beats Base on 11 of 12 (4 ties).
Figure 3a upstream knob comparison at matched FLOPs. Shape knobs move upstream loss somewhat, and upstream and downstream rankings differ (FF2K).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label was removed because it described untested parts. The Table 4 rows are a curated set of Pareto-efficient alternatives, not a random sample, and no uncertainty is reported, so small AVG differences (<0.3) are treated as ties. The steps value '219' is 2^19. Downstream rows use AVG of GLUE/SGLUE/SQuAD.

versions.untested_parts: Tests parameter/model-size relationships using T5 span-masked pretraining, not autoregressive cross-entropy; does not fit power laws or test token-count and compute scaling independently.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of much larger runs.
Does not find a loss-minimizing parameter/token split at fixed compute or estimate how parameter and token counts scale with compute.

The study varies depth and other shape choices and reports upstream shape effects, but does not provide a controlled, comprehensive fixed-parameter comparison across depth, width, and other architectural details.
The ViT experiments evaluate DeepNarrow few-shot image recognition efficiency, not power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.

Tests the relation between model size/pretraining performance and SuperGLUE downstream performance, plus selected fine-tuning results; does not establish predictability across downstream tasks generally.

Reports differences between upstream and downstream behavior and compute regions, but does not compare fitted exponents, parameter-counting choices, training schedules, or fitting methods, nor test whether curves bend away from a fitted power law.

rows.subject: dozen Transformers (Figure 1 aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Sampled within a two-order of magnitude band of model scales; configurations include XXXL (33B), XXL (11B), XL (3B), and LG (750M) with modified depths
rows.operation_detail: Compared pretraining negative log-perplexity across model sizes and shape variants, primarily varying depth
rows.measure: Negative log-perplexity versus model size and shape
rows.value: The text reports strong correlation with model size and weak dependence on model shape; no fitted exponent is reported.
rows.note: The aggregate textual result supports a size-related pretraining trend, but does not establish a power-law fit. The paper says it confirms weak upstream shape dependence.
rows.check: Condition 'steps: 219' is a text-extraction error for 2^19 (~524k) steps. For V4 the authors state upstream loss depends only weakly on shape, i.e. observed. For V1 it is partial: a strong monotone size trend over about two orders of magnitude, with no power-law fit and no token or compute axis.

rows.subject: dozen Transformers (Figure 1 aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Sampled within a two-order of magnitude band of model scales
rows.operation_detail: Compared SuperGLUE fine-tuning performance across model sizes and shape variants
rows.value: The strong pretraining correlation largely vanishes after fine-tuning; the text says downstream performance is not merely a function of parameter size.
rows.note: Aggregate description of the plotted model configurations; the paper does not give a correlation coefficient.
rows.check: State is correct for zoomed-in comparisons. The authors concede a general downstream trend may exist over very wide size ranges (Sec 4.1 'Zooming in Versus Zooming Out').

rows.subject: NL12-XXL
rows.operation_detail: Reported pretraining and downstream scores for this configuration

conditions.value: Downstream scores shown as three values; metric names not stated in the table

rows.measure: Pretraining negative log-perplexity and downstream scores
rows.note: The table reports three downstream values but does not label their metrics in the displayed columns.
rows.check: r3 and r4 should be read as one pair. NL12-XXL (3.6B) has better upstream negative log-perplexity (-1.46 vs -1.49) but lower downstream scores (85.1/76.5/88.1 vs 86.9/79.9/89.5). The three downstream values are likely GLUE/SGLUE/SQuAD, matching Table 4's column order.

rows.subject: NL32-XL
rows.operation_detail: Reported pretraining and downstream scores for this configuration

conditions.value: Downstream scores shown as three values; metric names not stated in the table

rows.measure: Pretraining negative log-perplexity and downstream scores
rows.note: The paper describes Table 3 as a counterexample to pretraining perplexity indicating transfer quality, but the displayed pair has the more favorable pretraining and downstream values together; the table does not label the three downstream metrics.
rows.check: The note is wrong: -1.49 is the worse negative log-perplexity. NL32-XL has worse upstream perplexity but better downstream scores than NL12-XXL, which is exactly the counterexample the paper states. This is the comparator for r3.

rows.subject: Mini-8L
rows.operation_detail: Compared a deepened Mini model with the canonical Small model
rows.note: A reported downstream comparison; the alternative has fewer parameters but a slightly lower AVG score.
rows.check: The smaller Mini-8L has worse ppl (-2.056 vs -2.021) and a marginally lower AVG (73.52 vs 73.57), consistent with size and loss. The state was mislabelled partial. Table 4 lists configurations selected as Pareto-efficient, so all of r5–r13 are a curated selection.

rows.subject: Small 16L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Small model and compared with the canonical Base model
rows.note: The paper also reports this configuration as faster and smaller than Base.
rows.check: Smaller model (134M vs 223M) with worse ppl (-1.825 vs -1.752) and lower AVG (78.73 vs 79.16). This is consistent with size and loss predicting downstream performance.

rows.subject: Small 20L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Small model and compared with the canonical Base model
rows.note: The score is slightly higher than Base; this is one of several depth configurations reported separately.
rows.check: 164M with worse ppl (-1.798) ties Base (79.30 vs 79.16). The size and loss gap does not show downstream; no uncertainty is reported.

rows.subject: Small 22L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Small model and compared with the canonical Base model
rows.note: The score is higher than Base; this is one of several depth configurations reported separately.
rows.check: 179M with worse ppl (-1.798 vs -1.752) exceeds Base AVG (79.54 vs 79.16). The margin is small and unreported for significance.

rows.subject: Small 24L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Small model and compared with the canonical Base model
rows.note: The text states that this model outperforms Base on all three listed downstream tasks.
rows.check: 193M with worse ppl (-1.783) beats 223M Base on all three tasks (AVG 79.92 vs 79.16).

rows.subject: Small 32EL
rows.operation_detail: Changed the encoder depth of a Small model and compared with the canonical Base model
rows.note: The score is higher than Base; this is an encoder-depth variant.
rows.check: 143M with much worse ppl (-1.897 vs -1.752) exceeds Base AVG (79.81 vs 79.16).

rows.subject: Base 36L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Base model and compared with the canonical Large model
rows.note: The score is nearly the same as Large; the text reports lower parameter and FLOP costs.
rows.check: 621M with worse ppl (-1.626 vs -1.605) ties 738M Large (82.89 vs 82.87).

rows.subject: Large 36L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of a Large model and compared with the canonical XL model
rows.note: The text says this model outperforms XL on all three downstream tasks.
rows.check: 1.1B with worse ppl (-1.564 vs -1.487) beats 2.9B XL on all three tasks (85.27 vs 84.38).

rows.subject: XL 32L
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth of an XL model and compared with the canonical XXL model
rows.note: The paper reports this model as about a third the size and about 44% of the FLOPs of XXL.
rows.check: 3.8B with worse ppl (-1.500 vs -1.430) matches 11.3B XXL (85.42 vs 85.20). The difference is small, but a model a third the size shows no deficit.

relationships.condition: T5 span-MLM upstream on C4, ~250M–30B params (Figure 1a)
relationships.reason: r1: the authors report a strong correlation of upstream negative log-perplexity with size, corroborating Kaplan. The trend is only qualitative, with no power-law fit.
relationships.display_finding: Upstream negative log-perplexity correlated strongly with model size, although the study did not fit a power law.

relationships.condition: Upstream pretraining perplexity, depth-varied models (Figure 1a, Table 3)
relationships.reason: r1: the authors confirm upstream performance depends weakly on shape. In Table 3, 3.6B vs 3.8B models of very different depth differ by only 0.03 in log-perplexity.
relationships.display_finding: Models with 3.6B and 3.8B parameters and very different depths differed by only 0.03 in log-perplexity.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned GLUE/SuperGLUE/SQuAD among models of nearby size ('zoomed in')
relationships.reason: r2: the size correlation largely vanishes downstream. In r3/r4, r8–r10 and r12, models with fewer parameters and worse pretraining perplexity match or beat larger ones downstream.
relationships.display_finding: Among nearby model sizes, downstream size correlations largely disappeared, and models with fewer parameters and worse perplexity matched or exceeded larger models on GLUE, SuperGLUE and SQuAD.

relationships.condition: Some neighbouring comparisons and wide size ranges
relationships.reason: r5 and r6 follow size and loss, while r7, r11 and r13 show ties despite size or loss gaps. The authors grant a general trend holds when zooming out over wide size ranges.
relationships.display_finding: Some comparisons follow model size and loss, while others tie despite differences in either, leaving a clearer general trend only across wider size ranges.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: T5 C4 span-masked pretraining across the Figure 1 size and depth configurations
reader_labels.reason: The authors report strong correlation between upstream negative log-perplexity and model size; r1 records this qualitative result, though it is not a fitted power law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The experiment uses one pretraining objective and schedule and does not fit an exponent or independently vary tokens and compute; r1 therefore supports only a narrower size trend.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that upstream performance depends weakly on model shape; r1 records the aggregate finding.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Figure 1 SuperGLUE comparisons across model sizes and shapes
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the strong upstream correlation largely vanishes after fine-tuning, so model size/pretraining performance did not reliably predict the reported downstream outcome; r2 records this result.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Reported downstream AVG scores vary across depth configurations: some are below the canonical comparator while others tie or exceed it; rows r5-r13 show the individually reported results.
